title: Temporary capacity reservoirs: billing reconciliation and operator controls
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Summary: This ticket designs and implements 'temporary capacity reservoirs' — a controlled transient capacity mechanism for Dedicated customers that allows predictable short-term throughput increases while ensuring transparent invoicing and operator controls. We will implement reservoir allocation, expiry/decay semantics, soft-taps for emergency capacity, and an overage reconciliation pipeline that avoids surprise invoices. The goal is to provide burstable throughput with clear economic rules and an operator UI to review/override events.

Background and motivation: Customers on Dedicated often need short-lived throughput increases for traffic spikes (e.g., product launches, marketing events). Current behaviors are a combination of autoscaling and quota borrowing; operationally these have led to three issues: 1) unpredictable per-minute scaling causing latency regressions, 2) opaque overage line items that customers dispute, and 3) insufficient operator visibility when bursts are manually allowed. Previous tickets introduced credit-like mechanisms and short-lived quotas, but reconciliation and manual controls remain partial.

Scope: Implement a platform-level transient capacity reservoir feature (not to be confused with long-term reserved capacity). Scope includes: 1) Reservoir creation and assignment logic (per-customer and global pool tiers), 2) Decay and expiry policy (time-based and usage-based), 3) API + SDK signals so SDKs/console can show available temporary capacity, 4) Overage billing path that produces itemized, auditable records and a grace/cushion period to reduce invoice disputes, 5) Operator console controls: preview of recent taps, manual revoke/extend, and audit trail with reason codes, 6) Reconciliation pipeline that links reservoir usage to the billing ledger and to metrics for SLO impacts.

Proposed design: Core concepts: Reservoir (temporary capacity allocation), Tap (a discrete consumption event against a reservoir), Cushion window (a short grace period after tap consumption during which downstream invoices are suppressed), and Arbitration record (reconciliation row used for billing/manual adjustments).

Allocation rules: - Customers can be granted reservoirs by policy (automatic: based on historical max QPS and plan tier; manual: ops grant). - Each reservoir has total_capacity_tokens, start_time, expiry_time, and decay_curve (linear by default). - Default reservoir sizes per tier are conservative; we will expose an admin API to tune.

Consumption & enforcement: - Serving runtime will prefer reservoir capacity for burst routing if available; if depleted or expired, requests follow normal dedicated capacity path and may incur overage. - KV cache and batching remain unchanged, but reservoir-aware scheduling will allow transient higher batch sizes for the tap window. - Soft-tap mode: when reservoir would be exceeded, a pre-authorized emergency allowance up to a per-customer soft cap may be used and recorded as a tap with 'soft' reason.

Billing and reconciliation: - Taps emit an AtomicUsageRecord into the transient_usage table (customer_id, reservoir_id, tap_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_used, reason_code). - We introduce a 'cushion window' (default 10 minutes) after tap closure where the billing system groups transient events for the same invoice period before charging; this reduces micro-line items. - All transient charges are labeled in invoices as 'temporary capacity' and include a link to the arbitration record in the console. - Reconciliation job (daily) computes final chargeable tokens per tap, applies any promo/waivers, and writes an Arbitration record that operators or customer billing teams can inspect. - We will add a lightweight disputes API for finance teams to raise an arbitration request tied to a tap.

Operator controls and observability: - Console: new Reservoirs panel under Dedicated > Capacity with recent taps, current capacity, expiry, and quick actions (revoke/extend/grant). - Audit: every operator action creates an immutable audit row with user, reason, and before/after capacity. - Alerts: we will create SLO alerts for reservoir exhaustion and for reservoir-driven latency increases. - Dashboards: per-customer time series for reservoir fill/deplete, tap frequency, and predicted next-day burst demand.

API/SDK changes: - Expose GET /v1/dedicated/{customer}/reservoirs and POST to request a temporary tap (name: /v1/dedicated/{customer}/reservoirs/tap). - Response fields include available_tokens, expires_at, and advisory_message. - SDKs will cache advisory_message for 1 minute and surface it to client apps as 'temporary_capacity_available'.

Migration and data: - Backfill: create synthetic reservoirs for customers that used transient credits last 6 months to preserve invoice continuity. - Billing migration: produce a mapping table from legacy transient events to new Tap records during the reconciliation window.

Testing and QA: - Unit tests for reservoir arithmetic, expiry, and decay. - Integration tests exercising tap->billing pipeline with simulated heavy traffic. - Load tests to validate runtime scheduling when reservoirs are tapped at scale. - End-to-end verification with staging billing pipeline and sample invoices.

Metrics and success criteria: - No increase in median 95th percentile latency during burst events compared to existing autoscaling baseline. - Reduction in invoice disputes related to burst capacity by 75% in first 60 days. - Operator time to resolve a transient billing dispute < 48 hours. - Drill: observe tap churn rate and ensure expected reservoir expiry behavior.

Rollout plan: 1) Internal alpha for SRE and small set of enterprise customers (2 weeks) 2) Gradual opt-in beta for customers on Dedicated (4 weeks) 3) Full launch and enable default per-tier reservoirs (6 weeks) 4) Monitor metrics and iterate.

Risks: - Incorrect reservoir accounting causing under/overcharging: mitigated by reconciliation job and daily audits during initial rollout. - Complexity in runtime scheduler impacting latency: mitigated by progressive canary and load testing. - Customer confusion: addressed via detailed invoice line items and console links.

Open questions: - Default cushion window length (10 min suggested) and whether it should be tier-configurable. - Soft-tap economics: should soft-taps be charged at a premium rate? (finance input needed) - How to expose reservoir forecasting to customers without leaking platform capacity signals.

Next actions: - Design review with billing and finance (EOD 2026-03-05) - Implementation spike for tap record schema and API (ownership: Ethan) - Dashboard mockups (ownership: Design)

Longer-term follow-ups: - Investigate scheduled reservoirs for planned events (e.g., product launches) - Integrate reservoir forecasts into Optimize to suggest customer's reservoir sizes
acceptance_criteria: Reservoir creation API and per-customer list implemented and instrumented
Transient tap records are written atomically by serving runtime and observable in console
Daily reconciliation job produces Arbitration records and maps to invoice line items
Operator console has review/extend/revoke actions with audit rows
Billing invoices include temporary capacity line items with links to arbitration records
